To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

small scale fisheries are a key element of the global food system, providing food for billions of people, and that the rights-based approach to fisheries governance provides an important framework for ensuring food and livelihood security for small scale fishing communities.
small scale fisheries are an essential part of the global food system, and that they are a key to achieving global and local food security and sustainable development.

small scale fisheries are important contributors to local and global human well being, and that the rights based approach is a promising framework for ensuring that these fisheries are recognized and supported in global and national level policy discussions about food security and food systems.
In summary, our research is concerned with

how the rights of small scale fishers to access, use, and manage marine and freshwater ecosystems are affected by the global food system, and how the rights of fishers can be used to improve the food security of small scale fishing communities.

how people’s food and livelihood security are connected to their engagement with marine and freshwater resources and ecosystems, and how these are connected to the larger political economic systems that govern fisheries.
how small scale fisheries are embedded in food systems and how these systems can be made more just and sustainable.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
small scale fisheries are a key part of food security at local and global scales, and that the concept of food security is incomplete without them.

fisheries, and smallscale fisheries in particular, have been and are important contributors to food security and livelihoods in many parts of the world, and that the role of fisheries in the global food system is under-recognized and under-valued.
small scale fisheries are an important part of food systems and security, and should not be left out of any discussions about food and food security.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

small scale fisheries are an essential element of food security and that the rights of small scale fishers and fishworkers must be recognized in order to ensure that these fisheries continue to be a vital part of the food systems of the future.
small scale fisheries are a critical component of food systems that are healthy, sustainable, and secure.
small scale fisheries, as an essential component of food systems, should be recognized and valued as an important source of food, jobs, livelihoods and culture.
The main takeaway from our work is that
fisheries are not only important in their own right, but also that the way that they contribute to people’s food and livelihoods, and the way they contribute to food security, are not always obvious.
the role of small scale fisheries in local and global food systems is much more important than it has been recognized in the past, and that this is an important area for future research and policy.

small scale fisheries are not only a source of food, but also a source of cultural identity, a context for the development of sustainable livelihoods and a way to connect the well being of people to the well being of marine and freshwater environments.
